title: Improve Dedicated Autoscaler: burst utilization reporting & priority routing adjustments
author: Avery Chen
description: Motivation: Customers on Dedicated capacity observed transient tail latency spikes and inaccurate fleet utilization metrics during burst windows. This PR improves burst accounting in the dedicated autoscaler and adds per-priority utilization reporting to help SREs tune tokenbucket and smoothing parameters. Summary: 1) Fix discrepancy in burst credit consumption ledger when requests are preempted by higher-priority traffic. 2) Add a new per-priority "burst_utilization" metric (percent of burst credits consumed over window) exported to metrics and the Console. 3) Surface a new autoscaler debug endpoint to fetch recent priority queue lengths and tokenbucket states for on-demand troubleshooting. 4) Update rollout to default-enable more conservative smoothing for existing fleets to reduce tail spikes. Checklist: - [x] Define metric and label schema (priority, fleet_id, region) - [x] Implement accounting fix and unit tests - [x] Add metrics exporter and Console wiring - [x] Add debug endpoint & API docs - [x] Update autoscaler default config and migration script - [x] End-to-end test in perf-canary Summary of changes: commits listed below. Testing: unit tests added for tokenbucket accounting edge cases; integration test in perf-canary showed 18% reduction in 95th percentile latency during synthetic burst; manual verification of Console dashboard rendering for new metric. Rollout plan: staged rollout to Dedicated fleets over 2 weeks: canary -> 20% -> 100%. Migration script included to apply conservative smoothing to older fleets; rollout is reversible and toggled via feature flag. Backwards compatibility: metric names are new; no breaking API changes. Related: ENG-1123 (autoscaler reliability), SUP-4421 (customer incident follow-up).
